status: all four mixed-training arms completed full-complex evaluation and paired comparisons; atom72 protein retention pending; balanced protein retention shows regression
scope: 16 official validation systems,32 conditions,256 forecasts per model; system paired bootstrap, seeds separate
matched_gq_comparison: Both balanced seeds improve bond error, RMSF error, center MSD error and both center/pocket energy scores relative to protein-only GQ2048 controls; marginal system-bootstrap CIs exclude zero in each of these comparisons.
pvb_comparison: Both seeds have better center/pocket energy scores, but markedly worse bond error; RMSF and center MSD differences are inconclusive. Not competitive overall.
chemistry_warning: Balanced71 still108.139 internal clashes/1000 ligand atoms and43.222 protein-ligand clashes/1000 ligand atoms; released PVB0.3743 and8.7798 with the same diagnostic. Bond improvement does not imply chemically usable trajectories.
causal_scope: Balanced versus GQ changes complex exposure plus role weighting. Both atom-average seeds improve complex geometry/motion versus GQ, supporting training-domain mismatch as a contributor. Balanced versus atom now has both matched seeds: weighting improves ligand bond error and center path energy score in both. It does not establish improved thermodynamics or protein retention.
weighting_uncertainty: Center MSD benefit is inconclusive in both seeds; RMSF benefit is inconclusive in71. Intervals are marginal, uncorrected for multiple metrics, and two seeds do not establish training-seed population effects.
decision: No default promotion: subsequent complete protein retention evaluation shows geometric regression in both balanced seeds and RMSF regression in seed72. See protein_retention_result.json. Complex-domain gains remain real but insufficient for a general-purpose model; ongoing shared-geometry and main-static experiments must repair this tradeoff. Remaining ligand internal geometry is a primary target.
limitations: Reused development systems and unknown parent/static exposure
Native PVB H1 versus Molvid H4 and unequal training budgets
